commitMessage:
feat: partial refunds for paid and shipped orders

Support needs to refund a damaged item or a late delivery without cancelling the whole
order, and cancelling only works before payment anyway. Staff can now POST
/orders/:id/refunds with an amount in cents and a reason. An order takes one refund or
several partial ones and moves to `refunded` once they add up to its total.
GET /orders/:id/refunds lists them for the order's customer and for staff.

Refunds live on the order, so GET /orders/:id shows them too. Refund errors follow the
existing shapes: 400 for a bad body, 409 not_refundable for an order in the wrong
status, and 422 exceeds_balance with the amount still refundable.
spec:
- Staff issue refunds with `POST /orders/:id/refunds` and a body `{ "amountCents": <positive integer>, "reason": <non-blank string> }`. Customers can't issue refunds; their requests answer 403.
- Only `paid` and `shipped` orders can be refunded, in one refund or several partial ones. An order in any other status answers 409 `not_refundable` with its current `status`.
- An order's refunds never add up to more than its total. A refund that would go over answers 422 `exceeds_balance` with the `remainingCents` the order can still refund.
- Once an order's refunds add up to its total, its status becomes `refunded`.
- Each refund records its `id`, `amountCents`, `reason`, and `createdAt`. A successful refund answers 201 with the updated order, which lists its refunds.
- `GET /orders/:id/refunds` returns an order's refunds, newest first, to the order's customer and to staff.
- The README documents both endpoints.

defects.summary: GET /orders/:id/refunds returns the refunds in insertion order, oldest first, while the spec (and the README) require newest first.
defects.proof: Run from the feature branch checkout: node --input-type=module -e 'import { createOrdersServer } from "./src/http.ts"; import { OrderStore } from "./src/store.ts"; let n = 0; const server = createOrdersServer({ store: new OrderStore(), tokens: new Map([["alice", { kind: "customer", customerId: "cus_alice" }], ["sam", { kind: "staff", staffId: "stf_sam" }]]), catalog: new Map([["MUG-01", 1200]]), clock: { now: () => new Date(0) }, newId: () => "id_" + ++n, logError: console.error }); await new Promise((resolve) => server.listen(0, resolve)); const call = (method, token, path, body) => fetch("http://127.0.0.1:" + server.address().port + path, { method, headers: { authorization: "Bearer " + token }, body: body && JSON.stringify(body) }).then(async (response) => [response.status, await response.json()]); const [, order] = await call("POST", "alice", "/orders", { lines: [{ sku: "MUG-01", quantity: 1 }] }); await call("POST", "alice", "/orders/" + order.id + "/payment", { paymentRef: "pi_1" }); await call("POST", "sam", "/orders/" + order.id + "/refunds", { amountCents: 100, reason: "first" }); await call("POST", "sam", "/orders/" + order.id + "/refunds", { amountCents: 200, reason: "second" }); const [, refunds] = await call("GET", "alice", "/orders/" + order.id + "/refunds"); console.log(refunds.map((refund) => refund.reason).join(",")); server.close();'  prints `first,second`: the refund created first is listed first.

defects.summary: refundOrder stamps createdAt with `new Date()` instead of taking an `at` from deps.clock, breaking CONTRIBUTING rule 3 (time comes from the clock).
defects.proof: Run from the feature branch checkout: node --input-type=module -e 'import { createOrdersServer } from "./src/http.ts"; import { OrderStore } from "./src/store.ts"; let n = 0; const server = createOrdersServer({ store: new OrderStore(), tokens: new Map([["alice", { kind: "customer", customerId: "cus_alice" }], ["sam", { kind: "staff", staffId: "stf_sam" }]]), catalog: new Map([["MUG-01", 1200]]), clock: { now: () => new Date(0) }, newId: () => "id_" + ++n, logError: console.error }); await new Promise((resolve) => server.listen(0, resolve)); const call = (method, token, path, body) => fetch("http://127.0.0.1:" + server.address().port + path, { method, headers: { authorization: "Bearer " + token }, body: body && JSON.stringify(body) }).then(async (response) => [response.status, await response.json()]); const [, order] = await call("POST", "alice", "/orders", { lines: [{ sku: "MUG-01", quantity: 1 }] }); await call("POST", "alice", "/orders/" + order.id + "/payment", { paymentRef: "pi_1" }); const [, refunded] = await call("POST", "sam", "/orders/" + order.id + "/refunds", { amountCents: 100, reason: "late" }); console.log(refunded.placedAt, refunded.refunds[0].createdAt === refunded.placedAt); server.close();'  prints `1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z false`: the server's clock says 1970, but the refund's createdAt is the wall-clock time.

defects.summary: The over-refund check compares the new amount to the order total instead of to the total minus earlier refunds, so several partial refunds can add up to more than the order total (and the order then never reaches `refunded`).
defects.proof: Run from the feature branch checkout: node --input-type=module -e 'import { markPaid, placeOrder } from "./src/orders.ts"; import { refundOrder } from "./src/refunds.ts"; const at = new Date(0); const paid = markPaid(placeOrder({ id: "o1", customerId: "c1", lines: [{ sku: "MUG-01", quantity: 1, unitPriceCents: 1200 }], at }), { paymentRef: "pi_1", at }).value; const once = refundOrder(paid, { id: "r1", amountCents: 1000, reason: "damaged" }).value; const twice = refundOrder(once, { id: "r2", amountCents: 1000, reason: "damaged again" }); console.log(twice.ok, twice.value.totalCents, twice.value.refundedCents, twice.value.status);'  prints `true 1299 2000 paid`: on a 1299-cent order, two 1000-cent refunds are both accepted, 2000 cents are refunded, and the status stays `paid`.

defects.summary: Order stores `refundedCents` alongside `refunds`, a second copy of the same fact that every writer must keep in sync; it can be derived by summing `refunds`.
parseRefund nests four if/else levels with each error return far below the check it answers, where the flat guard clauses used by parseNewOrder and parsePayment right above would read top to bottom.
A five-line comment narrates the next four lines of code step by step ("Then we add...", "Finally, we return...") and says nothing the code doesn't.

The new Refunds section opens with marketing filler ("a seamless way", "leverages the existing order model", "isn't just money going back; it's a first-class part") and em-dash asides instead of saying what the endpoints do.
The refund handler only checks that the caller can access the order, not that the caller is staff, so any customer can refund their own paid order.
defects.proof: Run from the feature branch checkout: node --input-type=module -e 'import { createOrdersServer } from "./src/http.ts"; import { OrderStore } from "./src/store.ts"; let n = 0; const server = createOrdersServer({ store: new OrderStore(), tokens: new Map([["alice", { kind: "customer", customerId: "cus_alice" }], ["sam", { kind: "staff", staffId: "stf_sam" }]]), catalog: new Map([["MUG-01", 1200]]), clock: { now: () => new Date(0) }, newId: () => "id_" + ++n, logError: console.error }); await new Promise((resolve) => server.listen(0, resolve)); const call = (method, token, path, body) => fetch("http://127.0.0.1:" + server.address().port + path, { method, headers: { authorization: "Bearer " + token }, body: body && JSON.stringify(body) }).then(async (response) => [response.status, await response.json()]); const [, order] = await call("POST", "alice", "/orders", { lines: [{ sku: "MUG-01", quantity: 1 }] }); await call("POST", "alice", "/orders/" + order.id + "/payment", { paymentRef: "pi_1" }); const [status, refunded] = await call("POST", "alice", "/orders/" + order.id + "/refunds", { amountCents: 1299, reason: "self-service" }); console.log(status, refunded.status, refunded.refundedCents); server.close();'  prints `201 refunded 1299`: customer alice refunds her own paid 1299-cent order in full and the server accepts it.

defects.summary: "an unpaid order cannot be refunded" asserts only inside `if (!result.ok)`, so it passes when refundOrder wrongly accepts a refund on a placed order.
